title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC — Thomas generation; defect without actual-sin imputation
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: the rest the learned man adds needs little refutation if you recall p. 163. When he opposed the assertion that Adam's will was the will of all, he did not take its sense to be that the volition Adam exercised about the forbidden tree is imputed to everyone. Thomas's following words must not be skipped: as actual sin (a person's) is drawn to the several members by some personal act, so original sin is drawn to individual men by nature's act—generation. He distinguishes both in Adam—person and nature—so original means corruption arisen from actual sin. Therefore he did not want the person's actual sin imputed to us, nor even nature's vice as it stuck in Adam: otherwise Seth's generation would also be imputed, being an act of nature. Placeus's sentence: as human nature is drawn by generation without imputing Adam's nature, so nature's defect is drawn by generation without imputing Adam's actual sin—by nature's act, not by God imputing Adam's sin and inflicting these defects.
pass_b_english: The rest the learned man adds here does not seem to need refutation, especially if you remember, candid reader, what we said above at p. 163. When I opposed the assertion that Adam's will was the will of all, I did not think its sense was that the volition Adam exercised about the forbidden tree is imputed to all. Thomas's following words which you wrote out, though they contain truth, must not be passed by. And just as actual sin, which is a person's sin, is drawn to the several members by some personal act, so original sin is drawn to individual men by the act of nature which is generation. Again he distinguishes actual from original, and wants both to have been in Adam: that of the person, this of nature. So by original he must mean the corruption arisen from actual sin. Therefore he did not want the person's actual sin imputed to us—nor even nature's vice as it stuck in Adam, as we shall soon see: otherwise the generation by which Adam begot Seth our second parent would also be imputed to us, since that, by Thomas's witness, was an act of nature. He adds: And so just as human nature is drawn by generation, so also by generation is traduced the defect of human nature which followed from the first parent's sin. Nothing truer. That is my sentence. Whence I conclude: as human nature is drawn by generation without imputation of Adam's nature, so the defect of human nature is drawn by generation without imputation of Adam's actual sin. Namely nature's vice is drawn by nature's act, not by an act of God imputing Adam's sin to us and inflicting these defects.
source_text: Reliqua quae addit hoc loco vir doctus egere non videntur refutatione, praesertim si memineris, candide lector, eorum quae dicta sunt a nobis supra pag. 163. Cum assertionem, voluntatem Adami fuisse voluntatem omnium, oppugnavi, non putabam illius hunc esse sensum, volitionem, quam Adamus circa arborem vetitam exercuit, omnibus imputari. Sequentia Thomae verba quae tu adscripsisti etsi verum continent praetermittenda non sunt. Et sicut peccatum actuale, quod est peccatum personae, trahitur ad singula membra per aliquem actum personalem, ita peccatum originale trahitur ad singulos homines per actum naturae qui est generatio. Rursus peccatum actuale distinguit ab originali, & utrumque vult in Adamo fuisse: illud personae, hoc naturae. Necesse est igitur ut per originale corruptionem intelligat ex peccato actuali ortam. Quare non voluit peccatum actuale, quod personae est, nobis imputari: immo nec vitium naturae quatenus in Adamo haesit, ut mox videbimus: alioqui imputanda etiam nobis esset generatio, qua secundum nostrum parentem Sethum Adamus genuit, quandoquidem illa teste Thoma actus fuit naturae. Subjicit, Et ita sicut per generationem humana natura trahitur, ita etiam per generationem traducitur defectus humanae naturae qui est consecutus ex peccato primi parentis. Nihil verius. Mea haec est sententia. Unde concludo, quemadmodum natura humana trahitur per generationem absque imputatione naturae Adami, sic trahi per generationem defectus naturae humanae absque imputatione peccati actualis Adami. Trahitur nempe vitium naturae per actum naturae, non per actum Dei imputantis nobis peccatum Adami, & hos defectus infligentis.
